title: feat(runtime): resolve a reference timezone onto ExecutionContext
body:
Closes #1978. Foundation slice of [ADR-0053 Phase 2](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/framework/pull/1975).

## What

Adds `ExecutionContext.timezone` (optional IANA zone) and resolves it **once per request** in `resolveExecutionContext`, with precedence **user preference → org default → `UTC`**:

- **User override** — `sys_user_preference` row `(user_id, key='timezone')`.
- **Org default** — the tenant-scoped `sys_setting` `(namespace='localization', key='timezone', scope='tenant')`. One org per physical tenant (ADR-0002), so the row needs no `tenant_id` filter.
- An invalid IANA zone is ignored and resolution falls through. Every read goes through the existing defensive `tryFind`, so timezone resolution **never blocks auth**.

## Why it's safe (pure plumbing, zero behavior change)

Nothing reads `ctx.timezone` yet, and an absent value resolves to `'UTC'` — exactly today's behavior. This is the keystone the rest of Phase 2 consumes:

- #1980 — tz-aware `today()`/`daysFromNow()`/`daysAgo()`
- #1981 — datetime rendering in the reference zone
- #1982 — tz-aware analytics bucketing

(Those slices depend on this one for the `timezone` value.)

## Notes

- A discoverable `localization` settings **manifest** for the org default is a small follow-up — the resolver already reads the row if present, so this lands without it.
- Resolution adds at most two cheap reads per authenticated request, consistent with the resolver's existing `sys_member` / permission-set lookups. A caching pass can come later if needed.

## Testing

- New: user preference wins over org default; tenant-scoped org default used when no user pref; `UTC` when neither; an invalid zone falls through; anonymous requests leave it unset.
- Full `@objectstack/runtime` suite green — **387 tests**; `@objectstack/spec` kernel green — **682**; DTS build + typecheck clean.
- Changeset: `minor` (new optional `ExecutionContext` field + resolver).
